analysis_steps.goal: Measure [C II] structural parameters via visibility modeling

method.value: Fit binned [C II] visibilities directly with 2D exponential disk models (1-component for single/multiple-UV, 2-component for pair/multiple-[C II]) and convert major-axis FWHM and axis ratio to circularized effective radius Re,[CII] and luminosity L_[CII].

evidence.quote: We used the `UVMULTIFIT` (Martí-Vidal et al. 2014) to model the visibilities of the [C ii] line emission in the CRISTAL sample.

For a 2-D exponential disk model, the major axis FWHM and major axis effective radius can be related as _R_ _e_,major = 1.21 × FWHM, therefore we obtained a circularized effective radius by calculating _R_ _e_,[CII] = 1.21 × FWHM √_q_, where _q_ is the minor-to-major axis ratio.

key_parameters.value: Sérsic index n = 1 (exponential disk); 6 free parameters (R.A., Decl., total flux density, major-axis FWHM, minor-to-major axis ratio q, position angle); q fixed to 1 when peak S/N < 8

evidence.quote: exponential disk model ( _n_ = 1) for all of the [C ii] components and first allow six parameters (R.A., Decl., total flux density, major-axis FWHM, minorto-major axis ratio, and position angle of major axis) free.

findings_qualitative.value: [C II] line emission is systematically more extended than rest-frame UV continuum (by a factor of 2.90 on average) and comparable to or more extended than FIR continuum (by a factor of 1.54 on average).

evidence.quote: We confirm that the [C ii] line emission is more spatially extended than the continuum emission, with average size ratios of ⟨_R_ _e_,[CII] /_R_ _e_,UV⟩ = 2.90 and ⟨_R_ _e_,[CII] /_R_ _e_,FIR⟩ = 1.54, although about half of the FIR-detected sample shows a comparable spatial extent between the [C ii] line and the FIR continuum emission (_R_ _e_,[CII] ≈ _R_ _e_,FIR).

findings_qualitative.value: The [C II] visibility profiles of individual and stacked single galaxies are well characterized by a single exponential disk without statistically significant evidence for a secondary extended [C II] halo component.

evidence.quote: To summarize, from the double component fitting in the stacked visibility data (Figure 7 right), we do not find a statistically significant evidence of [C ii] halo as a secondary component.
Based on Figure 6, 7, and 8, we conclude that the [C ii] line emission of the CRISTAL galaxies can be adequately explained by a single exponential disk component.

findings_qualitative.value: There is no statistically significant difference in [C II] sizes or size ratios between isolated single galaxies and interacting pair/multiple-UV systems.

evidence.quote: In spite of a variety of merger states, we do not statistically confirm the difference in [C ii] sizes between single and pair (_p_ value = 0.23)/multiple-UV (_p_ value = 0.12) systems.

findings_qualitative.value: [C II] surface density anti-correlates with rest-frame Ly-alpha equivalent width, while the [C II]-to-IR surface density ratio tentatively correlates positively with Ly-alpha equivalent width.

evidence.quote: We find a negative correlation between [C ii] surface density (Σ [CII]) and Lyα EW (_p_ value = 0.039), and a tentative positive correlation between [C ii]-to-IR surface density ratio (Σ [CII] /Σ IR) and Lyα EW (_p_ value = 0.090).

claims.hypothesis: [C II] line emission in star-forming galaxies at z = 4-6 is more spatially extended than rest-frame UV and FIR continuum emission.
claims.experiment: Model 2D exponential disk sizes of [C II] line emission directly in the uv-visibility plane using UVMULTIFIT for 34 components and compare with HST F160W (UV) and ALMA Band-7 (FIR) continuum sizes.
claims.result: [C II] effective radii range from 0.5 to 3.5 kpc with <Re,[CII]> = 1.90 +- 0.77 kpc, yielding average size ratios of <Re,[CII]/Re,UV> = 2.90 +- 1.40 and <Re,[CII]/Re,FIR> = 1.54 +- 0.63 (with two-thirds of FIR-detected sources having Re,[CII]/Re,FIR < 1.5).
claims.finding: [C II] emission is roughly twice as extended as star-forming regions traced by continuum emission, though about half of the FIR-detected sample has comparable [C II] and FIR extents explained by PDRs.

evidence.quote: We confirm that the [C ii] line emission is more spatially extended than the continuum emission, with average size ratios of ⟨_R_ _e_,[CII] /_R_ _e_,UV⟩ = 2.90 and ⟨_R_ _e_,[CII] /_R_ _e_,FIR⟩ = 1.54, although about half of the FIR-detected sample shows a comparable spatial extent between the [C ii] line and the FIR continuum emission (_R_ _e_,[CII] ≈ _R_ _e_,FIR).
In fact, we find that two-thirds of the sample (eight out of 12) shown in Figure 5 have comparable FIR continuum radius with [C ii] line radius (_R_ _e_,[CII] /_R_ _e_,FIR < 1.5).

claims.hypothesis: Star-forming galaxies at z = 4-6 possess a secondary extended 10-kpc scale '[C II] halo' component in addition to a central disk.
claims.experiment: Fit single and concentric double exponential disk models to individual and stacked visibilities of 16 isolated (single) galaxies and inspect normalized stacked residual visibilities.
claims.result: A single exponential disk (Re = 1.97 +- 0.10 kpc) fits the stacked visibility data as well as a double component model (same reduced chi^2), where the putative halo component (Re,halo = 9.17 +- 28.2 kpc) accounts for only 8.7 +- 13.4% of total flux (1.2 sigma excess at 20 klambda).
claims.finding: There is no statistically significant evidence for a secondary [C II] halo component; a single extended exponential disk adequately characterizes the [C II] emission.

evidence.quote: To summarize, from the double component fitting in the stacked visibility data (Figure 7 right), we do not find a statistically significant evidence of [C ii] halo as a secondary component.
Based on Figure 6, 7, and 8, we conclude that the [C ii] line emission of the CRISTAL galaxies can be adequately explained by a single exponential disk component.

claims.hypothesis: Ongoing galaxy mergers or star-formation-driven outflows drive the extended [C II] sizes and [C II]-to-UV size ratios.
claims.experiment: Compare [C II] size distributions between single, pair, and multiple-UV classes using Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests, and test for correlations between Re,[CII] or Re,[CII]/Re,UV and Sigma_SFR_IR using Spearman's rank correlation.
claims.result: KS test p-values are 0.23 (single vs pair) and 0.12 (single vs multiple-UV); Spearman rank p-values for correlations with Sigma_SFR_IR are 0.381 to 0.859.
claims.finding: No statistically significant difference in [C II] extent is found between isolated and merging systems, nor is there a significant correlation with SFR surface density that would link extended [C II] directly to ongoing outflows.

evidence.quote: Although we expect to find larger [C ii] sizes in pair and multiple-UV systems compared to single systems, we were unable to statistically distinguish their size distributions by performing the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test (with _p_ values of 0.23 and 0.12 for the pair and multiple-UV, respectively), largely due to our limited sample size.

Therefore, regardless of the merging events, we fail to rule out the null hypothesis that there is no association between star-formation-driven (atomic) outflows and the extended [C ii] line emission.

claims.hypothesis: The spatial extent and surface density of [C II] line emission are physically linked to neutral atomic gas and dust content, which regulate Ly-alpha escape.
claims.experiment: Test correlations of Sigma_[CII], Sigma_[CII]/Sigma_IR, and Re,[CII]/Re,UV against rest-frame EW_Lya.
claims.result: Sigma_[CII] negatively correlates with EW_Lya (r_s = -0.51, p = 0.039), Sigma_[CII]/Sigma_IR tentatively correlates positively with EW_Lya (r_s = 0.56, p = 0.090), and Re,[CII]/Re,UV shows a possible negative trend with EW_Lya (p = 0.516).
claims.finding: Higher dust and H I column densities increase [C II] surface density via photoelectric heating while attenuating Ly-alpha, supporting a scenario where diffuse atomic gas contributes to extended [C II] emission.

evidence.quote: We find a negative correlation between [C ii] surface density (Σ [CII]) and Lyα EW (_p_ value = 0.039), and a tentative positive correlation between [C ii]-to-IR surface density ratio (Σ [CII] /Σ IR) and Lyα EW (_p_ value = 0.090).

We also find a possible negative correlation between [C ii]-to-UV size ratio (_R_ _e_,[CII] /_R_ _e_,UV) and Lyα EW. If the correlation is real, this would support the scenario that extended [C ii] line emission at large radii is arising from the atomic gas component.

why_this_data.value: Combining compact and extended ALMA 12m configurations with archival ALPINE data provides both kpc-scale spatial resolution to separate interacting pairs and high sensitivity to large-scale extended structure.

evidence.quote: The combination of multi-configuration observations is essential to achieve both sufficiently large maximum recoverable scale (MRS) and high spatial resolution.
Therefore, we combined the data from the ALPINE Survey (#2017.1.00428.L) with the CRISTAL data to achieve better sensitivity to the extended structure.

why_this_method.value: Modeling directly in the interferometric visibility plane avoids image-domain biases at moderate S/N (noise fitting, clean beam smearing, dirty beam deviation from a single Gaussian) and avoids dependence on CLEAN imaging parameters.

evidence.quote: In such cases, the measured sizes in the image domain could be overestimated, because either the best-fit model takes noise into account, or the smearing effect of the clean beam affects the fittings (Tadaki et al. 2020; Mitsuhashi et al. 2024).

The visibility analysis is also favorable assessing faint extended features in [C ii] line emission, as the imaging procedure requires several parameters to be considered (e.g., weighting of visibility data, threshold, size of the masked region for the CLEAN algorithm) and therefore complicates the optimization of the best parameter sets (Jones et al. 2023).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Ongoing star-formation-driven outflows as the main driver of extended [C II] emission (rejected/unsupported due to lack of correlation with Sigma_SFR_IR)

evidence.quote: Therefore, regardless of the merging events, we fail to rule out the null hypothesis that there is no association between star-formation-driven (atomic) outflows and the extended [C ii] line emission.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Ionized gas as a dominant contributor to extended [C II] emission (inferred to have little impact, <~25%, based on stellar mass and metallicity relations)

evidence.quote: Since the majority of the CRISTAL galaxies have lower stellar masses than this, we infer that the [C ii] line flux contributed from the ionized medium is not as significant as ∼ 25 %, indicating that the contribution from ionized gas has little impact on the spatial extent of [C ii] line emission.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Radial variation in the central [C II] deficit causing larger apparent [C II] sizes than FIR continuum (rejected because stacked radial Sigma_[CII]/Sigma_IR profile is relatively flat)

evidence.loc: 4.3.3. [C ii ] deficit in the central region of galaxies
evidence.quote: In summary, we suggest that radial variation in the [C ii] deficit is not the primary cause of the extended [C ii] line emission.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Shock heating induced by galaxy mergers driving extended [C II] emission (rejected because merging systems show moderate Re,[CII]/Re,FIR ~ 0.7-1.5 or normal L_[CII]/L_IR ~ 3e-3)

evidence.quote: Shocked gas heating is not likely the driver of extended [C ii] line emission.

limitations_admitted.value: Multiplicity classification is morphological and does not incorporate kinematical state (e.g., CRISTAL-05 appears single in UV/[C II] morphology but is a line-of-sight pair kinematically), and some HST-single sources are pairs in sharper JWST images.

evidence.quote: We note, however, that this is still a crude classification, as we do not consider the dynamical state of each galaxy obtained from kinematical analysis.
three galaxies (CRISTAL-11, CRISTAL15, and CRISTAL-17) classified as single have pair-like morphology when looked with sharper images taken by James Webb Space Telescope

limitations_admitted.value: Limited sample size prevents statistically distinguishing [C II] size distributions across multiplicity classes and yields large uncertainties in size ratios.

evidence.quote: Although we expect to find larger [C ii] sizes in pair and multiple-UV systems compared to single systems, we were unable to statistically distinguish their size distributions by performing the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test (with _p_ values of 0.23 and 0.12 for the pair and multiple-UV, respectively), largely due to our limited sample size.

limitations_admitted.value: FIR continuum visibilities have lower S/N than [C II] and were modeled with a single circular exponential disk, preventing fair comparison in multiple-UV and multiple-[C II] systems and yielding an unreliable FIR size for CRISTAL-21.

evidence.loc: 3.2.2. Rest-frame UV and FIR continuum emission
evidence.quote: Unlike [C ii] line emission, all of the FIR continuum emission was fit in a single exponential disk component due to the lower S/N detection compared to the [C ii] line emission.
One galaxy that is well below the one-to-one line is CRISTAL-21, which has an unreliable FIR size measurement due to the insufficient S/N of the visibility data, particularly at short _uv_ distances.

limitations_admitted.value: Available Ly-alpha measurements come from slit spectroscopy and only probe global properties without spatial information.

evidence.loc: 4.4. Connection to Ly α and H α emission
evidence.quote: However, we note that the Lyα properties currently available are taken by slit spectroscopy (Cassata et al. 2020), and only global properties without spatial information can be inferred.

referee_caveats_inferred: Stacking visibilities of galaxies with diverse axis ratios (q = 0.31 - 0.90) without deprojecting or aligning major axes can artificially smear emission and mimic or dilute an extended halo.
Fixing the Sérsic index to n = 1 for all [C II] visibility fits could mask steeper or flatter inner/outer profiles that a free Sérsic index might capture.

Binned single-channel visibility fitting over +-2 sigma velocity width integrates over kinematic structures (rotation, tidal tails, outflows), potentially conflating kinematic extent with morphological extent.
